title: WebSocket protocol error path ignores client.showErrorDetails and leaks stack traces
body:
## Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

## Summary

When a malformed WebSocket `BackMsg` frame fails protobuf deserialization, Streamlit uses a path that bypasses uncaught app exception redaction. Because of this, `client.showErrorDetails` does not apply. Stack traces with file paths and line numbers can reach the client. I reproduced this on 1.61.1.

## Reproducible Code Example

```python
# app.py
import streamlit as st

st.write("hello")

# send_malformed_frame.py
import asyncio
import websockets


async def main():
    async with websockets.connect(
        "ws://localhost:8501/_stcore/stream",
        subprotocols=["streamlit"],
    ) as ws:
        # b"\\xff" is not a valid BackMsg protobuf frame.
        await ws.send(b"\\xff")


asyncio.run(main())
```

## Steps To Reproduce

1. Run `app.py` on Streamlit 1.61.1.
2. Set `client.showErrorDetails = "none"`.
3. In a second terminal, run `send_malformed_frame.py`.
4. The script connects to `ws://localhost:8501/_stcore/stream` with subprotocol `streamlit` and sends `b"\xff"`.
5. Observe that the script receives a `ForwardMsg` Exception payload.
6. Observe that the Exception payload contains `DecodeError` and a stack trace entry with an absolute file path.

## Expected Behavior

Protocol-level WebSocket errors should return a generic client error or close the connection. They should not expose stack traces, file paths, or line numbers to the client. `client.showErrorDetails` should not be bypassed.

## Current Behavior

The deserialization exception goes through `AppSession._create_exception_message()`. That method calls `exception_utils.marshall(...)` without `is_uncaught_app_exception=True`. The redaction logic does not run. On the event-loop thread there is no script run context, so traceback filtering does not remove internal frames. In my local repro, the returned Exception payload had message `Error parsing message with type 'BackMsg'`, type `DecodeError`, and a stack trace entry that exposed `lib/streamlit/web/server/starlette/starlette_websocket.py`.

## Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

## Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.61.1
- Python version: 3.12
- Operating System: Any
- Browser: N/A

## Additional Information

Split from [issue #16386](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/16386). This also affects the generic `AppSession.handle_backmsg()` exception path, not only protobuf deserialization failures.
